mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Municipal authority, utility service provider, or licensed bank of the residence country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if the source country has not acceded to the Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed credit institution or financial intermediary maintaining the UBO's banking relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (unless issued by a bank already subject to a Luxembourg recognized financial supervision regime; notarized signature acceptable as lower-tier confirmation)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power-of-attorney appointing the Luxembourg notary and corporate service provider for incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (notaire) countersigning with the foreign originator; attestation may be executed before a Luxembourg consul or apostilled if executed overseas
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / original execution before Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract from the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) of the originating corporate entity if any UBO is a company (corporate UBO cascading documentation, including articles of association and directors' registers)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) or foreign official corporate registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for foreign extracts; direct copy from LBR where applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under Luxembourg AML/CFT Law; electronic screening against OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated Security Council Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT Sanctions List, Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF) national references, and international adverse media/PEP databases. The natural persons UBOs, general partner, authorized signatories, and the corresponding beneficial owners of the corporate general partner (if any) must be screened. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), including family members and close associates, must undergo enhanced due diligence; source of wealth and source of funds documentation must be obtained for every PEP and for transactions requiring higher due diligence in the alcoholic beverage export trade.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be in French, German, Luxembourgish, or the Latin alphabet transliteration if the name originates in a non-Latin script (e.g., Chinese pinyin). The name must contain either the words 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp', or a faithful graphical representation, and must be clearly distinct from all existing RCS registrations. Official filings are executed in French, German, or Luxembourgish; any foreign trademark or brand component must be transliterated into Latin characters for RCS registration without pure Chinese characters in the corporate legal name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or its authorized representative may file a written request for reconsideration with the Registration Officer of the Luxembourg Business Registers within fifteen (15) days of the rejection notice. If the refusal is based on a substantial legal prohibition, the applicant may submit an administrative appeal before the administrative tribunal (Tribunal administratif) in Luxembourg City within three (3) months of the reconsideration denial. A commercial appeal (action en rectification) may also be commenced before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) to contest the registry's decision. Legal representation by a Luxembourg avocat is mandatory for formal court appeals.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or registered-agent-only address is accepted for an SCSp during the pre-incorporation period, but the entity is expected to have a physical presence and at least one local responsible person or domiciliation agent. Because the ISIC 4632 business is a wholesale export operation of alcoholic beverages, the Luxembourg authorities (notably the Ministry of Economy, the Administration de l'enregistrement et des domaines, and the RCS) will require proof of an operational office, storage/logistics arrangements or third-party warehouse contracts, and the ability to produce books and records. A mere virtual mailbox without any economic supervision will not satisfy the substance requirements for holding a commercial licence or for anti-abuse/anti-money-laundering validation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% annualized risk of an unannounced on-site inspection by the RCS registration officer or by the Administration des Douanes et Accises for the purposes of verifying excise goods trading, warehousing and transport documentation. The risk increases to approximately 30% if the UBOs are non-EU residents without independent professional management, or if the trade involves high volume movement of excise-bearing alcoholic beverages through third-party logistics.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as consolidated, Articles 12-1 to 12-9 (société en commandite spéciale, introduced by the Law of 13 July 2016); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register and the electronic publication of companies
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Luxembourg City
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'inscription au Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (electronic creation filing, RCS Form 01 / e-Desk application)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital: the SCSp is a contractual special limited partnership with freely determined capital; contributions may be in cash or in kind, and no statutory escrow or blocked-account requirement applies under Luxembourg law; a cash contribution is evidenced by a contribution certificate or bank credit letter.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED at the first meeting of the general partner of LU SCSP, a Luxembourg société en commandite spéciale under the Law of 10 August 1915, that: (i) the capital contributions subscribed under the partnership agreement be accepted, the capital being freely fixed with no statutory minimum; (ii) the registered office be established at the RCS-declared address; (iii) the general partner be confirmed as managing administrator, and its delegated natural person be appointed officer with sole signature power for banking, customs and export transactions; and (iv) the officer is instructed to file the spirits-excise and establishment-permit registrations without delay. Unanimously adopted and certified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and corporate denomination check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – online business names database (lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a preliminary search in the LBR database and the official trademark register for the proposed denomination 'LU SCSP' and any trade variants; if the denomination is not reserved, optionally file a name-reservation request through the LBR e-service to secure the exact corporate name pending the drafting of the partnership agreement.
required_dossiers: Requested denomination variants
Identity document of the requesting general partner
Power of attorney, if filed by a service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the denomination is not available because of identity or confusing similarity with an existing RCS or trademark entry, file a revised denomination including a distinctive element and re-submit the reservation request electronically the same day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: All partners (private deed); Luxembourg civil-law notary only where real property rights are contributed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the partnership agreement in French or German. The deed must state the identity of all general and limited partners, the capital and the form of each contribution, the profit-sharing schedule, the registered office address, the corporate object covering ISIC 4632 spirits export distribution, and the appointment of the general partner's delegate as manager. Sign in counterpart and consolidate a single original file for the subsequent RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement
Acceptance-by-all-partners clause or signature block
IDs and address proofs of partners
Contribution certificate or bank transfer confirmation for paid-up capital
Domiciliation or occupancy consent of the registered-office landlord
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A defective deed is cured by a rectification deed (acte rectificatif) signed by all partners, physically or by electronic signature, before the RCS filing is lodged; no penalty applies if filed within the same statutory month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS statutory registration and creation filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – Luxembourg Business Registers, electronic e-Desk portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of signature, lodge in the RCS e-Desk the electronic 'déclaration d'inscription – création' attaching the certified copy of the partnership agreement, the registered-office proof, the partner list, and the identification of the manager, choosing NACE/ISIC classification 4632. Upon admission, the applicant receives the RCS number, the Luxembourg registration number (matricule) and the insolvency-register notification.
required_dossiers: RCS electronic creation form (e-Form 01)
Certified copy of the partnership agreement
Certificate of registered office address
List of general and limited partners and amounts of subscriptions
Identity documents of manager(s) and declaration of admission of signature powers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS registrar issues a query for missing annexes or translation, respond within one month through the same e-Desk application; if the registrar rejects the filing, file a modified declaration with the observations cured; refusal may be appealed to the competent district court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) sitting on registration matters.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the official electronic companies gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA) – administrative publication managed by LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCS admission, the registrar automatically forwards the statutory legal particulars for publication in RESA, including the denomination, legal form, corporate object, registered office, identity of partners with unlimited liability and the manager; the publication establishes legal opposability and is a prerequisite to third-party reliance on the company's facts.
required_dossiers: RCS registration admission reference
Text blocks of the legal notice generated by the LBR system
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any clerical error in the RESA notice is corrected by an RCS amendment filing; the publication fee for the corrective notice is waived if raised within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial establishment licence for wholesale spirits export (autorisation d'établissement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale des Classes moyennes (Single Point of Contact, myGuichet.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the establishment-authorisation application on myGuichet.lu for wholesale trade of alcoholic beverages (ISIC 4632), covering the registered office and the managed storage operations; provide the RCS extract, good-repute evidence of the manager, and proof of appropriate professional capacity; the licence is issued within the statutory instruction period and is renewable upon any change of premises or manager.
required_dossiers: myGuichet establishment-licence application form
Current RCS extract and matricule number
Clean criminal-record extract of the manager (casier judiciaire)
Proof of professional qualification or 3 years of management experience in beverage distribution
Lease or ownership title of the operating premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A refusal notice may be challenged by hierarchical appeal to the Minister of the Economy within 40 days; if the Minister rejects, further recourse lies to the Tribunal administratif in Luxembourg City within 3 months of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Excise duty registration, VAT activation and SEED enrolment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des douanes et accises – Direction Accises, plus Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the matricule is allocated, the AEDT automatically preliminary-registers the SCSp for VAT; file the final VAT form and simultaneously register with the Customs and Excise Administration as a registered excise trader, and where applicable as warehousekeeper, to hold duty-suspended high-proof baijiu; supply the projected stock volumes in hectolitres of pure alcohol, the customs procedure codes for export, and the designated tax representative. A SEED number is then activated in the EMCS system.
required_dossiers: RCS extract and M-matricule certificate
Partnership agreement
VAT registration form (form 158)
Excise registration declaration with estimated hl-volume of pure alcohol
Layout and storage-capacity plan of the bonded or stock premises
Appointment of the excise contact person or tax representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the excise file is queried, furnish within one month a revised stocking plan, proof of the customs guarantee, and adjusted maximum-volume calculations; refusal of warehousekeeper status may be appealed to the Director of Customs and Excise within 3 months and subsequently to the administrative courts.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale des Classes moyennes (industrial and commercial establishment licensing) jointly with the Administration de l'environnement (classified establishments and environmental permits)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement – wholesale, warehousing and export distribution of high-proof traditional sorghum baijiu (wholesale spirits activity, ISIC 4632)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Classified establishment under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 May 2010: Class 4 – technical declaration and registration tier applicable to a spirits storage and distribution depot below the Seveso III lower threshold (≤ 50 t of flammable liquids); a full EIA report is not required, provided municipal zoning and the classified-establishment declaration are approved.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process effluent from wholesale operations; leakage-resistant containment within the storage basin; VOC emissions from ethanol storage to be vented via a controlled breather system not exceeding 20 g/m³ threshold; waste broken bottles and spill residues to be handled under the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management, with non-hazardous classification unless alcohol content exceeds the dangerous-substance concentration limits; firewater containment volume calculated in line with the Luxembourg fire-protection code for alcohol depots.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory fire-safety clearance delivered by the communal fire commission (Commission consultative des établissements classés) and the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) before commissioning; structural load-bearing approval of the warehouse floor and racking by an approved engineer; occupational workplace clearance issued by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering manual handling of glass bottles, ventilation, and the maximum permissible ethanol stock density per fire compartment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for VAT and excise; Administration des douanes et accises for customs and EORI. Portals: MyGuichet.lu (RCS and e-filing) and the AED e-filing system 'eCDF' for VAT returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Execute the SCSp limited partnership agreement (contrat de société), which may be in private writing unless real property is contributed. 2. File for registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through MyGuichet.lu; obtain the RCS number and the 8-digit national business number (NIF/matricule). 3. Submit the VAT registration form (Formulaire TVA 645) to the AED attaching the RCS extract, constitutional deed, and evidence of the gérant's (managing general partner's) powers; the AED issues the LU-prefixed VAT number within 2-4 weeks. 4. If the SCSp carries out customs operations, apply separately to the Administration des douanes et accises for an EORI number. 5. Non-EU-established partners with direct Luxembourg taxable supplies may require a VAT fiscal representative; the SCSp itself registers under its own name where it acts in its own name for VAT purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is mandatorily fiscally transparent for Luxembourg income tax purposes; there is no domestic check-the-box regime. Available elections: (i) upon unanimous request of all partners, the SCSp may irrevocably opt under Article 175bis LIR to be treated as a taxable corporation (corporate income tax and municipal business tax), but the option is restricted by the ATAD I/II implementation and is generally inadvisable for a cross-border export platform; (ii) hybrid mismatch alignment elections under Article 168sexies LIR allow the SCSp to align its transparency classification with a foreign jurisdiction to avoid deduction/non-inclusion mismatches; (iii) a VAT grouping election under Article 60 of the Luxembourg VAT Law permits the SCSp to join a Luxembourg VAT group as a single taxable person.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Luxembourg Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA), governed by the amended law of 12 February 1979 transposing Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Non-established foreign entities: no registration threshold — mandatory VAT registration from the first taxable transaction in Luxembourg. Luxembourg-established entities: annual turnover exemption of EUR 35,000 under Article 57 of the VAT Law, but the small business exemption does not cover export-linked supplies and is excluded for entities engaged in VAT-exempt export operations needing input VAT recovery; in practice an exporting SCSp registers from inception.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-based pre-clearance, or digital stamping regime applies in Luxembourg as of 2025. B2B e-invoicing is voluntary (subject to customer consent). E-invoicing via PEPPOL is mandatory only for B2G invoices to Luxembourg public-sector entities. VAT returns, EC Sales Lists, and Intrastat declarations are filed electronically through the AED's eCDF portal on a monthly or quarterly periodicity. The EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) framework is expected to introduce mandatory e-invoicing and digital transaction reporting for intra-EU B2B supplies from 2030, but no such mandate is currently operative.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Article 51(1) of the Luxembourg VAT Law (transposing Article 146(1)(a) of the VAT Directive) applies to Baijiu quantities physically dispatched or transported by the SCSp or on its behalf to a destination outside the EU customs territory. The SCSp must demonstrate that the goods left the EU within 90 days of dispatch (extendable to one year on substantive justification), hold the customs export declaration, and retain transport and payment evidence in its VAT records. Zero-rating is denied where goods are merely sold while inside the EU or where export documentation is incomplete; the place of supply rules are also relevant where the SCSp acts as an intermediary for Baijiu never entering Luxembourg.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document, IM/EX) validated electronically or stamped by customs
Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill (AWB), or CMR consignment note evidencing physical dispatch to a non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank payment confirmation / SWIFT MT103) evidencing receipt of export consideration from the foreign buyer
Commercial Invoice detailing the Baijiu consignment (quantity, ABV proof strength, FOB/CIF value)
Excise movement document (e-AD) and customs exit confirmation evidencing discharge of excise duty upon export
EORI number proof and, where applicable, Intrastat/DEB declarations for any intra-EU components
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AED may retrospectively claw back zero-rating and re-assess VAT at the 16% standard rate on the export consideration, with default interest of 0.6% per month and a 10% additional tax (droit en sus). Administrative fines for incorrect declarations or false documentation reach EUR 25,000 under Article 67 of the VAT Law. Intentional fraud triggers criminal tax fraud sanctions under the Luxembourg General Tax Law (Steueranpassungsgesetz) of up to twice the evaded tax and/or imprisonment of the managing general partner. The standard VAT assessment period is 5 years, extended to 10 years for fraud. Given the SCSp's fiscally transparent nature, VAT debts, penalties, and clawbacks may be recovered directly from the partners, and joint and several liability may arise for the gérant under Article 205 of the VAT Directive in cross-border chain transactions where the entity knew or should have known of the export-irregularity.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as the integrated financial and AML supervisor; Ministry of Finance for financial-services legislation; no separate foreign-exchange administration exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible; Luxembourg applies the EU free movement of capital and payments (Article 63 TFEU), allowing unrestricted current and capital account transactions. Profit remittance by the SCSp is not subject to exchange control approval or scheduled convertibility restrictions. Any practical exit depends on the bank's AML/KYC verification and tax documentation rather than FX permission. The SCSp is fiscally transparent, so profit distribution follows the partnership agreement and the partners' tax residence; no Luxembourg booking of retained export proceeds is blocked unless a sanctions or freezing measure applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory export-proceeds surrender, minimum conversion ratio, or retention timeline applies in Luxembourg/Eurozone. Exporters may keep CNY, USD or other permitted currencies in an authorised credit institution. Cross-border trade settlements are subject only to ordinary BCL/CSSF reporting, including monthly balance-of-payments statistical declarations by resident banks for large flows, customer due diligence, and suspicious transaction reporting to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to moderate. Offshore digital EMIs without a Luxembourg or EEA authorisation cannot lawfully provide EUR IBAN accounts or access TARGET2/SEPA clearing. An EEA-authorised EMI can be used for ancillary multi-currency FX conversion, but EMIs generally do not issue documentary letters of credit and many reject partnerships or distributors of alcoholic beverages under trade-based AML risk policy. The SCSp should therefore treat EMIs as a supplementary operational rail, never the primary clearing or escrow rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory rule requires a physical interview for all entities, but Luxembourg banks' CDD policies commonly require an in-person meeting with the general partner's representatives and any non-EEA ultimate beneficial owner. Remote eIDAS-based video identification may be accepted for EEA residents; non-EEA owners should expect a physical interview or notarised and apostilled identity verification. Directors, UBOs and mandate signatories must provide passports, proof of residential address and corporate authorisations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque SCSp holding structure with non-EEA Chinese investors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified partnership agreement, LBR/RCS registration extract, UBO register (RBE) confirmation, investor identification documents, aggregate share schedule showing economic ownership, source-of-wealth statement and corporate reference letters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Licensed alcoholic-beverage export industry perceived as trade-based money-laundering channel
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid Luxembourg wholesale liquor/beverage distribution licence; Chinese producers' supply contracts; pro-forma and commercial invoices; customs and EUR1/cl/INV declarations; warehouse receipts; transport and insurance docs; end-client KYC/import licences.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large initial capital contribution into a zero-minimum-capital SCSp
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed capital contribution/share subscription agreement, board or partner resolutions, bank statement showing provenance of funds, investor tax identification, employment/business/tax records evidencing accumulated wealth, and an affidavit of no encumbrance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party counterparty payments and commission fee routing affecting export transactions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contemporaneous trade contract, counterparty UBO/KYC pack, shipping documents, inspection certificates, letter-of-credit terms, exact invoice-beneficiary matching, and a written rationale for any commission or third-party settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Thin substance or virtual-office profile for SCSp in Luxembourg
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease contract, access to office infrastructure, payroll or outsourced management agreements, director interview records, regulatory licence held locally, bookkeeping service agreement and annual account filings; the stability of the anticipated trade flow supporting real presence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 EUR transfers from the investor's bank to the SCSp's BCL/CSSF-regulated bank account. The beneficiary reference should state 'Capital contribution - [investor name] - [SCSp RCS number]'. Banks require the economic purpose and will report the payment under Luxembourg balance-of-payments statistics, using the category for direct investment/equity capital; commercial prepayments must be classified as trade credits. Supporting verification includes the signed capital commitment or subscription agreement, Luxembourg corporate authorisation, UBO declarations, proof of source of funds, and a Chinese outbound investment/filing confirmation where applicable. No central bank approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements, the SCSp should primarily use EUR SWIFT MT103 payments for direct disbursements to Chinese distilleries, freight and insurance. For larger, higher-risk shipments, obtain a documentary commercial letter of credit issued by BIL/BCEE/BNP through the SWIFT MT700 series, with advising and confirming banks in China. Revolving or standby LCs can service repeated Baijiu supply contracts. All disbursements must be matched against purchase orders, commercial invoices, customs valuations, bills of lading/airway bills, insurance certificates and, where used, LC compliance documents such as inspection and phytosanitary certificates.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/CNY outright forwards with a Luxembourg/EEA credit institution or licensed investment firm
EUR/CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for trade flows where offshore CNY availability or deliverability is constrained
EUR/CNY cross-currency swaps for medium-term inventory financing under ISDA/CSA and EMIR transaction reporting
Vanilla EUR/CNY FX options and zero-cost collars used solely to hedge firm trade commitments, subject to bank credit lines and EMIR mitigation rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual financial statements (comptes annuels) with the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS), District Court of Luxembourg
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the end of the financial year; for a calendar year entity, no later than 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file exposes the manager(s) to a formal notice, administrative fines of up to EUR 5,000, coercive daily fines of EUR 25 to EUR 500 per day, and, after two consecutive years of default, judicial dissolution or administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership register declaration update (RBE confirmation) aligned with annual cryptographic review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Event-driven filing within 30 days after any transfer or change in beneficial ownership; no-separate no-change declaration is legally due but an annual internal certification is performed by 31 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing of a required change is punishable by fines of EUR 50 to EUR 1,000 per offence, increased for intentional submission of false data, potentially including imprisonment; repeated default may trigger publication by the AML authority and restriction of public procurement eligibility.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the accuracy of registered particulars and statutory partner register (corporate secretarial certification)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) – internal record after director scrutiny
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No separate RCS filing required unless a change occurred; the confirmation is completed internally and filed with the minute book no later than 30 June each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incorrect or stale registered information may lead to a fine of EUR 100 to EUR 1,000 under the RCS Law and could preclude the accused entity from participating in certain contracts; material untruths may trigger administrative investigation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory audit for an SCSp is triggered if for two consecutive financial years it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds: total balance-sheet assets EUR 4.4 million; net annual turnover EUR 8.8 million; average workforce 50 full-time employees. Entities exceeding these limits must appoint an independent approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 23 September 2011 on accounting obligations as amended, transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU; optional application of IFRS is available when required for consolidated reporting or upon designated regulatory approval.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg law mandates that the beneficial owner register (RBE) be filed within 30 days of any share transfer or ownership change. There is no statutory annual no-change filing. The SCSp nevertheless adopts an annual governance procedure by 31 January: the general partner reviews the internal register, reconciles it with the filed RBE record, signs a corporate certification, and files any required corrective declaration with the RCS.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Partner and Manager Resolutions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% (standard CIT for profits above EUR 200,000); 24.94% aggregate rate in Luxembourg City including municipal business tax and solidarity surcharge
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is tax-transparent: no corporate income tax, municipal business tax, or solidarity surcharge at entity level; partners are taxed on their share. Qualifying participation exemption (100% on dividends/capital gains), 80% IP income exemption, and full interest deduction; loss carryforward of 5 years applies to opaque corporate taxpayers, while transparent SCSp allocates current losses to partners.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 700/710 (partnership/corporate income tax declaration), e-filed via MyGuichet.lu with a valid LuxTrust e-ID.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end; extension up to 6 months upon request; steady calendar-year filing for all entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS number, Luxembourg tax ID, address, legal form (SCSp), and date of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate all non-resident partners and their countries of residence in the annex; provide their foreign tax IDs when available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the fiscal year; exact accounting reference period; any short or first-year period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the same fiscal-year dates as the SCSp financial statements; align with the partnership agreement's accounting period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net pre-tax profit or loss per the audited/unaudited financial statements before partner allocations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report amounts in EUR; foreign partners must receive their allocable share in the SCSp's functional currency, translated to EUR.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back non-deductible expenses (fines, non-arm's-length payments, excessive management fees); deduct tax-exempt income (participation exemption, IP box exemption, foreign PE relief).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners may only claim adjustments related to Luxembourg-source income (PE, real estate) or items expressly covered by a tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of profit/loss to each partner according to the SCSp agreement; include each partner's name, RCS/TIN, percentage share, and amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign partners report their Luxembourg PE income on separate non-resident returns; no dividend withholding tax applies to a transparent SCSp distribution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine up to EUR 10,000; monthly late-payment interest 0.6%; default surcharge up to 10% of assessed tax; false declarations attract criminal penalties up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% for dividends paid by a Luxembourg fully taxable corporate entity; SCSp distributions are not dividends and are outside WHT. If the SCSp opts for opaque corporate taxation, distributions are subject to 15% WHT (0% under parent-subsidiary privilege or applicable DTA).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief (e.g., China–Luxembourg treaty: 5% dividend rate for ≥25% holdings; 0% interest/royalties), the non-resident beneficial owner must deliver a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) to the Luxembourg payer before the payment date. The payer may apply reduced WHT at source; alternatively the non-resident may file a refund claim with the Administration des Contributions Directes within five years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic royalty WHT: 0%; domestic interest WHT: 0% (no source WHT on arm's-length interest). DTA rates typically 0%; an exceptional 10% WHT may apply on payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions as listed by Luxembourg law.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 500,000 annual value of related-party transactions (goods/services/financial) triggers a mandatory Local File; groups with consolidated revenue above EUR 750 million must also file a Country-by-Country Report and Master File.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No standalone Luxembourg ESR code; however, the ATAD GAAR and the OECD/Cadbury-Schweppes jurisprudence require real economic substance to claim treaty benefits and deduct intercompany expenses. An SCSp exporting baijiu must maintain local substance: registered office, local management decisions, operational staff, a Luxembourg bank account, and supporting contractual evidence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully submitting false income declarations, omitting sales revenue, fabricating invoices, or deliberately understating taxable profit in Luxembourg tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years under Luxembourg General Tax Law and Criminal Code Art. 391; additional civil penalties of up to 100% of evaded tax plus 0.6% monthly interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers/directors who sign false returns are personally liable for evaded taxes, civil restitution, criminal fines, travel bans, and imprisonment; the corporate veil is pierced for fraudulent acts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SCSp merely as a booking vehicle without real management, staff, premises, or substantive export-trading functions to obtain treaty or tax-treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits; recharacterization of income; additional CIT/municipal tax up to 24.94%; penalties up to 10% of the reassessed tax; in egregious cases, judicial dissolution under Luxembourg company law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable for resulting tax assessments and unlawful distributions; travel bans and director disqualification can follow where fraud or negligence is shown.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the baijiu export distribution business without the required alcohol licence, failing to perform KYC/CDD on clients and beneficial owners, or failing to register real beneficiaries with the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 1 million under Luxembourg AML law; criminal sanctions up to EUR 500,000 and 5 years' imprisonment; revocation of licence and debanking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML compliance officers and directors face personal criminal liability, pecuniary sanctions, director disqualification up to 10 years, and travel bans for serious breaches.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain contemporaneous TP documentation or pricing baijiu export transactions with affiliates not at arm's length, shifting profits to low-tax jurisdictions without operational substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment by the Luxembourg tax authorities, plus 0.6% monthly late-payment interest; separate penalty up to EUR 25,000 for missing documentation; criminal tax fraud sanctions if wilful.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false TP documentation are exposed to criminal conviction, personal civil liability for the group's tax exposure, travel restrictions, and imprisonment.
